title: Experimental investigation of solar biomass hybrid dryer for drying large cardamom in the north‐eastern Himalayan state Sikkim
content:
Abstract

Sikkim, a state in northeastern India, is a leading producer of large cardamom (Amomum subulatum Roxburgh). A solar biomass hybrid (SBH) dryer with a drying capacity of 20 kg per batch was developed. In the absence of sunshine, the biomass gasifier acts as a backup supply of heat energy. Within 20 h, the moisture level could be lowered from an initial 82.3% moisture content to a final 10% moisture content by maintaining the drying temperature between 50 and 70°C. The air velocity during drying was maintained at approximately 0.70 m/s. The experimental results showed that the SBH dryer's drying efficiency was 35.84%, with a drying rate varying between 0.4 and 0.6 kg/h. The biomass gasifier consumed about 0.5 kg of biomass for every kg of dried material. A net reduction in drying time of about 80.76% and 33.39% respectively, was observed when compared to open sun drying and conventional furnace (Bhatti). The solar-dried and open sun-dried samples had an oil concentration of 2.91% and 3.08% respectively, while the Bhatti dried sample had the lowest at 1.5%. The SBH dryer exhibited the lowest extraneous matter (2.13%) compared to the open sun-dried sample (3.78%) and traditional Bhatti (2.22%). The SBH dryer exhibited a minimal color change of 2.06, in contrast to the furnace (Bhatti) dried samples at 6.21 and the open-dried samples at 2.63. The developed SBH dryer was found to be suitable for northeast hilly regions, providing uninterrupted drying for small-scale farmers in rural areas.
